Query libSQL as the signed-in user

Source: R/backend__libsql.R
oauth_db_libsql_api.Rd

Run SQLite SQL against a remote libSQL or compatible Turso endpoint using the visitor's current access token. Results are returned as data frames.

Usage

oauth_db_libsql_api(
  authorization,
  url,
  target = NULL,
  required_scopes = character(),
  min_valid_for = 60,
  timeout = 30,
  ca_bundle = NULL,
  session = shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()
)

Arguments

authorization

auth$connection from a shinyOAuth server module, without parentheses. To select a saved authorization, pass a function that calls auth$connection(id).

url

HTTPS database base URL, or a libsql:// URL (uses HTTPS). A reverse proxy path is allowed; omit /v2/pipeline.

target

Token target name in the shinyOAuth client. NULL uses its default token, including for clients without named targets.

required_scopes

Additional permissions to check before use. Request consent and set the client's permission requirements in shinyOAuth.

min_valid_for

Minimum remaining token lifetime, in seconds, when obtaining a token. Use 0 to accept any unexpired token.

timeout

Maximum seconds for one HTTP operation.

ca_bundle

Optional trusted CA certificate bundle path.

session

Shiny session. Inferred when the helper is created in server().

Value

An R6 client with these methods:

  • $query(sql, parameters = list(), raw = FALSE) returns a data frame, or a validated Hrana statement result with raw = TRUE.

  • $execute(sql, parameters = list()) runs one statement and invisibly returns its Hrana result, including affected_row_count and last_insert_rowid.

Details

The server must accept the access token issued to your shinyOAuth client. Self-hosted libSQL uses Ed25519 signing keys and libSQL permission claims; arbitrary OIDC access tokens are not interchangeable with database tokens. Turso Cloud has a separate external-provider JWKS configuration. See vignette("libsql", package = "shinyOAuthDB") for both configurations.

Each operation obtains a current token and uses a new Hrana HTTP stream, closing it in the same request. No stream baton or server-provided URL is reused. Calls cannot share transactions, temporary tables or connection state. The helper does not provide a DBI connection or embedded replica.

Create the helper inside server() and call its methods in render or reactive expressions. Results arriving after account changes, permission loss or sign-out are discarded. Requests use verified HTTPS and never retry, including after HTTP 401. A submitted statement may continue on the server after a timeout or sign-out.

Parameters and results

Supply an unnamed list for ? parameters or a fully named list for named parameters such as :country. Values are bound separately from SQL. Character, logical, integer, finite numeric, raw vectors and NULL/NA are supported. Use I("9223372036854775807") for an exact signed 64-bit integer; ordinary character values bind as text. Encode dates as strings.

SQLite integers are returned as strings to preserve all 64 bits. Floating point values remain numeric; non-finite results become NaN. Text remains character and blobs use raw vectors in list columns. Columns with mixed SQLite types remain lists. All-null or empty columns use logical missing values; raw = TRUE preserves the server's declared column metadata.

See also

vignette("libsql", package = "shinyOAuthDB"). oauth_db_demo() runs a local libSQL and Keycloak example.

Other platform API clients: oauth_db_bigquery_api(), oauth_db_clickhouse_api(), oauth_db_cratedb_api(), oauth_db_databricks_api(), oauth_db_fabric_api(), oauth_db_opensearch_api(), oauth_db_oracle_ords_api(), oauth_db_postgrest_api(), oauth_db_salesforce_api(), oauth_db_salesforce_data_cloud_api(), oauth_db_supabase_api()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
libsql <- oauth_db_libsql_api(auth$connection, "https://sqlite.example.org")
output$rows <- shiny::renderTable({
  libsql$query("SELECT id, total FROM orders WHERE country = :country LIMIT 20",
    parameters = list(country = "NL"))
})
} # }
